precepts.why:
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and Solomon says what he made it of: “For thy Almighty hand, that made the world of matter.” The world was made of matter.

In science matter is anything that takes up space and has mass, meaning it has volume and can be weighed; any substance that exists and can be physically touched. It is composed of atoms, too small to see with your eyes, and exists as solid, liquid or gas. A rock, water and the human body are all matter. Matter is broken down into pure substances and mixtures, and the pure substances are the elements and compounds. God created the earth from matter, and God created man from matter.

points: for never wouldest thou have made any thing, if thou hadst hated it: so it says never wouldest thou have made anything if thou hatest it. Hold that and get Romans 9 verse 13 real quick.
and abhorrest nothing which thou hast made: and you don't hate anything that you made.

And how could any thing have endured, if it had not been thy will: that's the point. How could anything have endured if it had not been thy will? So like we read, he created the evil, the wicked, and all that for his sword. How can we be put on slave ships if that wasn't his will? He said in Deuteronomy 28:68, You shall go into Egypt again with ships. It was God's will to punish us for our evil.

or been preserved, if not called by thee: nothing could have been preserved if it wasn't called by him. Think about it. How did they ship millions of us across the planet earth and we were preserved through that? That was the Lord's will too.
for they are thine, O Lord, thou lover of souls: they are thine. Who is thine? The elect of God, the Israelites.

The Egyptians were deceived into worshipping serpents void of reason and vile beasts. God sent unreasonable beasts against them for vengeance, so that they would know a man can be punished by the very thing with which he sins. The creatures they honoured became part of their punishment.

The Almighty hand made the world from matter without form. God did not lack the power to send multitudes of bears or fierce lions. His choice of creatures for a judgment is not limited by his ability.

“Or unknown wild beasts, full of rage, newly created”. Esau thinks he has seen everything, but Solomon, the wisest man, speaks of unknown creatures. They are full of rage; you cannot pacify them or tell them to roll over and play dead. They breathe fiery vapour or filthy scents of scattered smoke and shoot horrible sparkles from their eyes. The ideas behind creatures such as Godzilla did not come from nowhere; men have been reading these scriptures.

Their harm can destroy people, and even the terrible sight can do so. That is why seeing the heavenly beasts could make a person's spirit leave him. God has strange creations in heaven and earth we have not beheld. Think of the angler fish deep in the sea, with great teeth and a light on an antenna: that is only a glimpse of what is below, not proof that we have found it all.
